_note: Pinned trust roots for external ledger anchors (lib/anchor-verify.mjs, docs/VERIFY.md 'External anchors'). A verifier trusts these keys, never a copy of a root carried inside a token. Check the fingerprints below against the issuer's own publication before relying on them; a bank deployment passes its auditor's TSA root with --tsa-root.

tsa.name: DigiCert Trusted Root G4
tsa.for: http://timestamp.digicert.com (responder 'DigiCert SHA256 RSA4096 Timestamp Responder 2026 1' via 'DigiCert Trusted G4 TimeStamping RSA4096 SHA256 2025 CA1')
tsa.source: Mozilla CA root store as shipped in Node.js v22.17.0 (tls.rootCertificates), extracted 2026-09-29; DigiCert publishes the same root at https://cacerts.digicert.com/DigiCertTrustedRootG4.crt

rekor.name: rekor.sigstore.dev (Sigstore public-good transparency log)
rekor.source: https://rekor.sigstore.dev/api/v1/log/publicKey, fetched 2026-09-29; the same key is distributed in the Sigstore TUF root (sigstore/root-signing, trusted_root.json tlogs[].publicKey)
